```{r}
locate_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  repeat {
    if (
      file.exists(file.path(candidate, "renv.lock")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(candidate, "_quarto.yml"))
    ) {
      return(candidate)
    }
    parent <- dirname(candidate)
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) {
      stop("Could not locate the project root", call. = FALSE)
    }
    candidate <- parent
  }
}

compact_gt <- function(
  data,
  groupname_col = NULL,
  source_note = NULL,
  font_size = 12
) {
  output <- gt::gt(data, groupname_col = groupname_col) |>
    gt::opt_row_striping() |>
    gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "—") |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.width = gt::pct(100),
      table.font.size = gt::px(font_size),
      data_row.padding = gt::px(4),
      column_labels.font.weight = "600",
      heading.align = "left",
      source_notes.font.size = gt::px(10.5),
      row_group.padding = gt::px(4)
    )
  if (!is.null(source_note)) {
    output <- output |>
      gt::tab_source_note(gt::md(source_note))
  }
  output
}

format_p <- function(value) {
  nh_format_p_value(value)
}

format_p_pair <- function(raw, adjusted, bold_adjusted) {
  raw_text <- format_p(raw)
  adjusted_text <- format_p(adjusted)
  adjusted_text <- ifelse(
    !is.na(bold_adjusted) & bold_adjusted,
    paste0("**", adjusted_text, "**"),
    adjusted_text
  )
  paste0("p = ", raw_text, "; q = ", adjusted_text)
}

format_effect_values <- function(
  estimate,
  lower,
  upper,
  effect_scale,
  metric_slot,
  result_status
) {
  result <- rep("—", length(estimate))
  non_estimable <- result_status == "NON_ESTIMABLE_COMPONENT_FAILURE"
  result[non_estimable] <- "Not estimable"

  mder <- metric_slot == 15L & !is.na(estimate)
  result[mder] <- sprintf(
    "%+.3f (%+.3f to %+.3f)",
    estimate[mder],
    lower[mder],
    upper[mder]
  )

  ratio <- grepl("ratio", effect_scale, fixed = TRUE) &
    !mder & !non_estimable & !is.na(estimate)
  result[ratio] <- sprintf(
    "%.2f× (%.2f to %.2f)",
    estimate[ratio],
    lower[ratio],
    upper[ratio]
  )

  absolute <- !ratio & !mder & !non_estimable & !is.na(estimate)
  result[absolute] <- sprintf(
    "%+.2f h (%+.2f to %+.2f)",
    estimate[absolute],
    lower[absolute],
    upper[absolute]
  )
  result
}

format_effect <- function(data) {
  format_effect_values(
    data$estimate,
    data$lower_95,
    data$upper_95,
    data$effect_scale,
    data$metric_slot,
    data$result_status
  )
}

format_sample <- function(days, participants, sites) {
  sprintf(
    "%d days / %d participants / %d sites",
    days,
    participants,
    sites
  )
}

category_label <- function(category) {
  dplyr::recode(
    category,
    `level-based` = "Light level",
    `duration-based` = "Duration and continuous periods",
    `timing-based` = "Timing",
    `exposure-history-based` = "Exposure history",
    `spectrum-based` = "Spectrum"
  )
}

primary_table <- function(predictor_id) {
  table_data <- primary |>
    filter(.data$predictor_id == predictor_id) |>
    mutate(
      Category = category_label(.data$manuscript_category),
      Metric = .data$manuscript_name,
      `Effect (95% CI)` = format_effect_values(
        .data$estimate,
        .data$lower_95,
        .data$upper_95,
        .data$effect_scale,
        .data$metric_slot,
        .data$result_status
      ),
      `Exact fitted sample` = format_sample(
        .data$participant_days,
        .data$participants,
        .data$sites
      ),
      `Association p / FDR q` = format_p_pair(
        .data$association_raw_p_value,
        .data$association_bh_adjusted_p_value,
        .data$association_fdr_supported &
          .data$association_h01_claim_eligible
      ),
      `Site-interaction p / FDR q` = format_p_pair(
        .data$site_heterogeneity_raw_p_value,
        .data$site_heterogeneity_bh_adjusted_p_value,
        .data$site_heterogeneity_fdr_supported &
          .data$site_heterogeneity_h01_claim_eligible
      ),
      Assessment = case_when(
        .data$metric_slot == 3L ~ "Non-estimable two-part result",
        .data$metric_slot == 15L ~ "MDER result; no association FDR support",
        .data$association_fdr_supported &
          .data$association_h01_claim_eligible ~
            "FDR-supported; limitations apply",
        TRUE ~ "No association FDR support; limitations apply"
      )
    ) |>
    select(
      Category,
      Metric,
      `Effect (95% CI)`,
      `Exact fitted sample`,
      `Association p / FDR q`,
      `Site-interaction p / FDR q`,
      Assessment
    )

  table_data |>
    compact_gt(
      groupname_col = "Category",
      source_note = paste(
        "Effects use metric-specific scales; all intervals are pointwise 95% CIs, not simultaneous intervals.",
        "Bold q-values meet the explicitly labelled FDR q < 0.05 rule and",
        "the explicitly labelled claim-eligibility rule. Timing site interactions remain",
        "sensitivity-dependent even when their q-value is below 0.05."
      ),
      font_size = 10.5
    ) |>
    gt::fmt_markdown(
      columns = c(`Association p / FDR q`, `Site-interaction p / FDR q`)
    ) |>
    gt::cols_width(
      Metric ~ gt::px(205),
      `Effect (95% CI)` ~ gt::px(175),
      `Exact fitted sample` ~ gt::px(160),
      `Association p / FDR q` ~ gt::px(125),
      `Site-interaction p / FDR q` ~ gt::px(125),
      Assessment ~ gt::px(190)
    ) |>
    gt::cols_align(
      "center",
      columns = c(
        `Effect (95% CI)`,
        `Exact fitted sample`,
        `Association p / FDR q`,
        `Site-interaction p / FDR q`
      )
    )
}

placement_table <- function(predictor_id) {
  table_data <- placement |>
    filter(.data$predictor_id == .env$predictor_id) |>
    mutate(
      Category = category_label(.data$manuscript_category),
      Metric = .data$manuscript_name,
      Result = paste0(
        format_effect_values(
          .data$estimate,
          .data$lower_95,
          .data$upper_95,
          .data$effect_scale,
          .data$metric_slot,
          .data$result_status
        ),
        "; n = ",
        format_sample(.data$participant_days, .data$participants, .data$sites)
      )
    ) |>
    select(
      metric_slot,
      Category,
      Metric,
      scenario_label,
      Result
    ) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = scenario_label, values_from = Result) |>
    arrange(.data$metric_slot) |>
    select(-metric_slot)

  table_data |>
    compact_gt(
      groupname_col = "Category",
      source_note = paste(
        "Each cell is the estimate (pointwise 95% CI, not a simultaneous interval) followed by its exact",
        "participant-days, participants, and sites. Chest and common-day placement",
        "results are estimation-only complements; no additional p-value family",
        "was created."
      ),
      font_size = 9.2
    ) |>
    gt::cols_width(
      Metric ~ gt::px(190),
      gt::everything() ~ gt::px(235)
    )
}

format_primary_cell <- function(data) {
  effect <- format_effect_values(
    data$estimate,
    data$lower_95,
    data$upper_95,
    data$effect_scale,
    data$metric_slot,
    data$result_status
  )
  q_value <- format_p(data$association_bh_adjusted_p_value)
  q_value <- ifelse(
    data$association_fdr_supported & data$association_h01_claim_eligible,
    paste0("**q = ", q_value, "**"),
    paste0("q = ", q_value)
  )
  ifelse(
    data$metric_slot == 3L,
    "Not estimable; q = —",
    paste0(
      effect,
      "<br>",
      q_value,
      "; ",
      data$participant_days,
      " days / ",
      data$participants,
      " participants"
    )
  )
}

primary_matrix_table <- function() {
  table_data <- primary |>
    mutate(
      Category = category_label(.data$manuscript_category),
      Metric = .data$manuscript_name,
      Context = recode(
        .data$predictor_id,
        work_free_day = "Free / Work",
        activity_status = "Active / Sedentary",
        previous_sleep_duration_centered_h = "+1 h previous sleep"
      ),
      Result = format_primary_cell(pick(everything()))
    ) |>
    select(metric_slot, Category, Metric, Context, Result) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Context, values_from = Result) |>
    arrange(.data$metric_slot) |>
    select(-metric_slot)

  table_data |>
    compact_gt(
      groupname_col = "Category",
      source_note = paste(
        "Primary near-eye predictor-specific participant-day models.",
        "Each cell gives the estimate with its 95% CI, FDR-adjusted q-value within",
        "the 15-outcome family, and exact fitted participant-days and participants.",
        "Bold q-values meet the FDR criterion. All analyses use nine sites."
      ),
      font_size = 12
    ) |>
    gt::fmt_markdown(columns = c(`Free / Work`, `Active / Sedentary`, `+1 h previous sleep`)) |>
    gt::cols_width(
      Metric ~ gt::px(220),
      gt::all_of(c("Free / Work", "Active / Sedentary", "+1 h previous sleep")) ~
        gt::px(250)
    )
}

format_global_q <- function(value) {
  paste0("**q = ", format_p(value), "**")
}

format_equal_site_contrast <- function(estimate, lower, upper) {
  sprintf("**%.2f×** (%.2f to %.2f)", estimate, lower, upper)
}

format_comparison_model_cell <- function(
  estimate,
  lower,
  upper,
  uses_interaction,
  site_minimum,
  site_maximum,
  association_q,
  interaction_q
) {
  model_text <- ifelse(
    uses_interaction,
    "Interaction model: site-average full contrast",
    "Additive model: common contrast"
  )
  site_text <- ifelse(
    uses_interaction,
    sprintf(
      "<br><small>Full site-specific ratios: %.2f to %.2f</small>",
      site_minimum,
      site_maximum
    ),
    ""
  )
  paste0(
    "**",
    model_text,
    "**<br>",
    sprintf("%.2f times (%.2f to %.2f)", estimate, lower, upper),
    site_text,
    "<br><small>Additive-family association q = ",
    format_p(association_q),
    "; global site-interaction q = ",
    format_p(interaction_q),
    "</small>"
  )
}

format_joint_effect <- function(

}
```

## Scientific question

The signed hypothesis states: **“Day type (weekday/weekend; free/work day),
daily exercise, and sleep variables predict daily light exposure metrics.”**
This complementary analysis asks that question with one row per admissible
metric-specific participant-day. It does not give days with more supported
hours greater weight.

The completed [hourly H06 analysis](H06.qmd) is the selected main H06 result.
This participant-day analysis is complementary, preregistration-oriented
evidence. The two analyses are related but have different outcomes and
weighting; neither result substitutes for the other. The
[analysis-preparation and provenance companion](../../audit/hypotheses/H06_daily/H06_daily_analysis_preparation.qmd)
documents the exact inputs, models, checks, and stored outputs used here.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false" title="Answer in brief"}

In the primary near-eye analysis, false-discovery-rate (FDR) adjustment, which
limits the expected proportion of false discoveries within each prespecified
15-slot family, retained associations for **10 of 14 estimable metrics** with
Free versus Work day,
**6 of 14** with Active versus Sedentary status, and **12 of 14** per
additional hour of previous-night sleep. Every retained association requires
the model-check qualifications (model diagnostics), which assess fit, support,
residual behavior, and sensitivity evidence, described below.

For outcomes fitted as $\log_{10}(Y + 0.1)$, $Y$ remains in its stated unit,
such as lx for melEDI, h for continuous periods, or lx h for dose. The
back-transformed ratios compare fitted geometric-mean-like values of $Y + 0.1$;
they are not ratios of raw metric means.

- Free days had lower fitted mean melEDI, M10 mean, waking time above 250 lx
  melEDI, longest continuous period above 250 lx melEDI, and melEDI dose than
  Work days. M10 and L10 midpoints and first light above 250 lx melEDI were
  later, whereas last light above 250 lx melEDI was earlier.
- Active days had higher fitted mean melEDI, M10 mean, time above 1,000 and
  250 lx melEDI, longest continuous period above 250 lx melEDI, and melEDI
  dose than Sedentary days.
- Longer previous-night sleep was associated with lower fitted light-level,
  bright-duration, longest-period, and dose metrics; more time below 1 lx
  melEDI during sleep; and later M10, L10, mean-light, and first-light timing.

Ten primary predictor-by-site interaction blocks, which allow an association
to differ among sites, met their separate 15-slot FDR rule. For example, the
interaction model estimated lower Free-day mean melEDI at every site, with
pointwise 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) excluding 1 at Dortmund (DE),
Tübingen (DE), Madrid (ES), and Kumasi (GH). A pointwise interval assesses one
site estimate at a time and is not a simultaneous band. The global interaction
test establishes variation across sites, while the site intervals describe
where the fitted site-specific contrasts are clearest.

In the exploratory mutually adjusted daily models, activity estimates were
stable after adding day type and sleep. Three sleep estimates and four
work/free estimates shifted by 1 to less than 2 standard errors. One
work/free estimate, time below 1 lx melEDI during sleep, reversed direction
and shifted by more than 3 standard errors. Mean melEDI nevertheless remained
lower on Free days after adjustment, with a fitted ratio of 0.75 (95% CI 0.68
to 0.82; FDR q < 0.001).

The separate nonlinear generalized additive mixed model (GAMM) analysis of
30-minute bins allowed context associations to vary smoothly over clock time
while accounting for repeated measurements. It found time-varying profiles for
day type, activity, within-participant sleep, and between-participant sleep in
its four-test exploratory FDR family. The selected main hourly H06 analysis
does not give the same answer as the daily mean metric: hourly melEDI was higher
on Free days, whereas the participant-day mean metric was lower. This
difference is scientifically plausible because the analyses use different
outcomes, weighting, and model structures.

The overall two-part L10 mean result remains non-estimable, and all three
primary MDER 95% intervals included zero. The gap-timing-unaware analysis is
reported only as a sensitivity.

:::

## Data and analysis

### Outcomes, contexts, and sample roles

The 15 participant-day outcomes comprise mean melEDI; M10 and L10 mean
melEDI; four threshold-duration measures; the longest continuous period above
250 lx melEDI; M10 and L10 midpoint; mean, first, and last timing above 250 lx
melEDI; melEDI dose; and melanopic daylight efficacy ratio (MDER). “Period”
describes the continuous-duration metric. Sleep-period light is interpreted as
the bedside sleep environment, not verified ocular exposure.

The three primary contexts were:

- Free versus Work day;
- Active versus Sedentary daily activity status; and
- each additional hour of previous-night sleep duration, centered at 8 h.

Near-eye measurements are primary. All-available chest results are a
complementary non-ocular comparison. Paired/common results compare the two
placements after retaining the same participant-days in both placements. More
generally, a common sample means that the compared models or placements use the
same participant-days. The gap-timing-unaware dataset repeats the near-eye
analysis as a separate metric-construction sensitivity.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h06-daily-analysis-roles
#| tbl-cap: "Analysis roles and exact fitted-sample ranges."

role_descriptions <- c(
  "Primary near eye, all available" =
    "Primary daily-metric estimates and six primary FDR families",
  "Complementary chest, all available" =
    "Complementary placement estimates; no additional p-value family",
  "Paired/common near eye" =
    "Near-eye estimates on common placement days",
  "Paired/common chest" =
    "Chest estimates on the same common placement days",
  "Gap-timing-unaware near eye, all available" =
    "Separate sensitivity estimates and six separate FDR families"
)

sample_roles |>
  mutate(
    `Analysis role` = unname(role_descriptions[.data$scenario_label]),
    `Participant-days` = if_else(
      .data$minimum_participant_days == .data$maximum_participant_days,
      as.character(.data$minimum_participant_days),
      paste0(
        .data$minimum_participant_days,
        "–",
        .data$maximum_participant_days
      )
    ),
    Participants = if_else(
      .data$minimum_participants == .data$maximum_participants,
      as.character(.data$minimum_participants),
      paste0(.data$minimum_participants, "–", .data$maximum_participants)
    ),
    Sites = if_else(
      .data$minimum_sites == .data$maximum_sites,
      as.character(.data$minimum_sites),
      paste0(.data$minimum_sites, "–", .data$maximum_sites)
    )
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Scenario = .data$scenario_label,
    `Analysis role`,
    `Participant-days`,
    Participants,
    Sites
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste(
      "Ranges arise because every metric × predictor result uses its exact",
      "complete fitted frame. Exact denominators accompany every result below."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Scenario ~ gt::px(235),
    `Analysis role` ~ gt::px(420),
    gt::everything() ~ gt::px(110)
  ) |>
  gt::cols_align(
    "center",
    columns = c(`Participant-days`, Participants, Sites)
  )
```

The nine study sites, in display order, are
`r paste(site_registry$display_name, collapse = ", ")`. Primary near-eye
results use all nine sites; the complementary chest and paired/common results
use eight sites where both the placement and exact metric-specific frame are
supported.

### Models, contrasts, and multiplicity

The non-timing outcomes use fixed study-site terms and a participant random
intercept, which allows participants to have different baseline outcome
levels. The primary models were fitted separately for each predictor, so
their estimates are not mutually adjusted for the other two day-level
contexts. The common-association and predictor-by-site interaction formulas are:

```text
response ~ site + predictor + (1 | participant)
response ~ site * predictor + (1 | participant)
```

Four clock outcomes, M10 midpoint, L10 midpoint, first timing above 250 lx
melEDI, and last timing above 250 lx melEDI, use the corresponding fixed-site
linear models with participant-cluster HC3 uncertainty. All displayed
intervals are **pointwise 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs)**; each assesses
one estimate at a time, and none is simultaneous. A site-average estimate gives
each included site equal weight, irrespective of its observed sample size.

Multiplicity comprises 12 separate FDR families: primary
and gap-timing-unaware datasets × three predictors × association or
predictor-by-site interaction. Every family retains all 15 named metric
slots. L10 mean remains the non-estimable slot 3 with missing raw and adjusted
p-values; MDER occupies slot 15 and has no association FDR support.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h06-daily-fdr-families
#| tbl-cap: "Twelve fixed 15-slot FDR families."

family_summary |>
  mutate(
    Dataset = recode(
      .data$dataset_id,
      primary = "Primary",
      gap_timing_unaware = "Gap-timing-unaware"
    ),
    Predictor = .data$reader_name,
    Test = recode(
      .data$test_type,
      association = "Association",
      site_heterogeneity = "Predictor-by-site interaction"
    ),
    `Family valid` = if_else(.data$family_construct_valid, "Yes", "No")
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Dataset,
    Predictor,
    Test,
    `Named slots` = .data$named_slots,
    `Estimable slots` = .data$estimable_slots,
    `FDR-supported` = .data$fdr_supported_slots,
    `Claim-eligible` = .data$claim_eligible_slots,
    `Family valid`
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    groupname_col = "Dataset",
    source_note = paste(
      "FDR-supported counts are numerical q < 0.05 decisions.",
      "Claim-eligible counts additionally exclude MDER and",
      "retain all stated model-check limitations."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::cols_align(
    "center",
    columns = c(
      `Named slots`,
      `Estimable slots`,
      `FDR-supported`,
      `Claim-eligible`,
      `Family valid`
    )
  )
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false" title="How to read the estimates"}

- A **site-average estimate** gives every included site equal weight. It is not
  weighted by the number of observations contributed by each site.
- A **predictor-by-site interaction** allows the association between a context
  and an outcome to differ among sites. A global interaction test does not by
  itself identify which site estimates differ.
- A **pointwise 95% CI** describes uncertainty for one displayed estimate. It
  is not a simultaneous interval across sites, metrics, or clock times.
- An **FDR adjustment** limits the expected proportion of false discoveries
  among the tests in its explicitly defined family.
- A **participant random intercept** allows participants to have different
  baseline outcome levels. A **common sample** retains the same participant-days
  across the compared models or placements.
- **Model checks** cover fit, support, residual behavior, and sensitivity
  evidence. A working first-order autoregressive correlation, **AR(1)**, allows
  adjacent residuals within a participant-day sequence to be correlated.

:::

### Supported predictor-by-site interactions

Ten global predictor-by-site interaction blocks met the separate 15-slot FDR
rule. A retained global interaction indicates that the predictor association
varies across sites. It does not identify a pair of sites that differ. The
table first gives the **site-average comparison-versus-reference contrast from
the complete interaction model**, with every site weighted equally. For these
ratio-scale outcomes, it is the geometric mean of the nine full site-specific
ratios. The site entries then show adjustment factors relative to that
site-average contrast:

\[
\text{site adjustment factor}
=
\frac{\text{full site-specific comparison/reference ratio}}
{\text{site-average comparison/reference ratio}}.
\]

An adjustment factor below 1 means that the site's fitted ratio is lower than
the site-average ratio; a factor above 1 means it is higher. Multiplying the
site-average ratio by the adjustment factor recovers the site's full fitted
ratio. The pointwise intervals localize the fitted pattern, but they are not
separately multiplicity adjusted and are not pairwise site comparisons.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h06-daily-primary-site-interactions
#| tbl-cap: "Site-average contrasts and site adjustment factors for primary interaction blocks retained by the global FDR rule."
#| column: page

primary_site_summary |>
  mutate(
    Predictor = .data$predictor,
    Metric = .data$manuscript_name,
    `Global interaction FDR q` = format_global_q(.data$global_interaction_bh_q),
    `Site-average comparison / reference` = format_equal_site_contrast(
      .data$equal_site_display_estimate,
      .data$equal_site_display_lower_95,
      .data$equal_site_display_upper_95
    ),
    `Site adjustment below site average; pointwise 95% CI excludes 1` =
      .data$pointwise_adjustment_below_equal_site,
    `Site adjustment above site average; pointwise 95% CI excludes 1` =
      .data$pointwise_adjustment_above_equal_site,
    `Site adjustment compatible with site average; pointwise 95% CI includes 1` =
      .data$pointwise_adjustment_compatible_with_equal_site
  ) |>
  select(
    Predictor,
    Metric,
    `Global interaction FDR q`,
    `Site-average comparison / reference`,
    `Site adjustment below site average; pointwise 95% CI excludes 1`,
    `Site adjustment above site average; pointwise 95% CI excludes 1`,
    `Site adjustment compatible with site average; pointwise 95% CI includes 1`
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    groupname_col = "Predictor",
    source_note = paste(
      "Batch: primary near-eye predictor-specific interaction models.",
      "The site-average column gives the equal-weight comparison/reference ratio from the",
      "complete interaction model: Free/Work, Active/Sedentary, or per",
      "additional hour of previous-night sleep. Each site adjustment is its",
      "full site-specific ratio divided by that site-average ratio; multiply the",
      "two to recover the full site-specific ratio. Site intervals are",
      "unadjusted pointwise 95% CIs and do not test one site against another.",
      "The bold q-value is the global interaction-block test. Filled dots use",
      "consistent study-site colors and do not encode significance."
    ),
    font_size = 8.7
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = gt::everything()) |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Metric ~ gt::px(205),
    `Global interaction FDR q` ~ gt::px(100),
    `Site-average comparison / reference` ~ gt::px(165),
    `Site adjustment below site average; pointwise 95% CI excludes 1` ~
      gt::px(300),
    `Site adjustment above site average; pointwise 95% CI excludes 1` ~
      gt::px(300),
    `Site adjustment compatible with site average; pointwise 95% CI includes 1` ~ gt::px(330)
  )
```

For the author’s mean-melEDI example, the site-average Free/Work ratio from the
interaction model was 0.70 (95% CI 0.63 to 0.78), with every site weighted
equally. Delft (NL) had a pointwise higher site adjustment, 1.36 (1.01 to 1.83),
meaning a weaker Free-day reduction than the site-average pattern. Madrid (ES),
0.71 (0.56 to 0.90), and Kumasi (GH), 0.57 (0.43 to 0.76), had pointwise lower
adjustments, meaning stronger reductions. The remaining six adjustment
intervals included 1. For example, the full fitted Delft (NL) ratio is
0.70 × 1.36 = 0.95, apart from rounding.

![Site deviations from the site-average context association.](../../artifacts/10_figures/H06_daily/H06_daily_stage3_primary_site_deviations.png){#fig-h06-daily-primary-site-deviations fig-alt="Ten faceted forest plots show nine site adjustment factors for each globally supported primary predictor-by-site interaction. A factor below 1 means the site's comparison-to-reference ratio is lower than the equal-weight site-average ratio, and a factor above 1 means it is higher. Horizontal bars are pointwise 95% confidence intervals. Of 90 site adjustments, 13 are pointwise below 1, 11 are pointwise above 1, and 66 include 1. Filled points use consistent study-site colors and do not encode significance." width="100%"}

[Source data for the site-deviation figure](../../artifacts/11_source_data/H06_daily/H06_daily_stage3_primary_site_deviation_figure.csv)

[Complete site-specific interaction estimates](../../artifacts/11_source_data/H06_daily/H06_daily_stage3_primary_site_interaction_estimates.csv)

The L10 occurrence component had complete or quasi-complete separation, so the
overall two-part association and predictor-by-site interaction tests were not
estimable. Positive-only and regularized component model checks do not replace
that overall result. MDER is the arithmetic mean of viable positive finite
one-minute melEDI/illuminance ratios; its primary estimates were −0.001 for
Free versus Work day (95% CI −0.013 to 0.011), 0.008 for Active versus
Sedentary (−0.007 to 0.024), and 0.002 per additional hour of sleep (−0.003 to
0.006).

## Gap-timing-unaware sensitivity

The separate gap-timing-unaware families retained 10, 6, and 13
claim-eligible FDR-supported associations for Work versus Free day, activity
status, and previous-night sleep, respectively. The broad pattern therefore
persisted. Exactly three association decisions differed from the primary
dataset:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h06-daily-gap-decision-changes

gap_changes |>
  mutate(
```

The longest continuous period above 250 lx melEDI was FDR-supported only in
the primary Work/Free analysis. Mean timing above 250 lx melEDI for Work/Free

## Exploratory mutually adjusted daily analysis

This exploratory batch directly addresses whether day type, activity, and
previous-night sleep remain stable when included together. For each metric,
one common complete-case near-eye frame was used for both the separate
predictor models and the mutually adjusted model. For the 14 estimable metrics,
this common sample contains 715 participant-days from 137 participants. Using
the same rows prevents a sample change from being mistaken for covariate
adjustment.

For non-timing outcomes, the mutually adjusted formula was:

```text
response ~ site + day type + activity + previous-night sleep +
  (1 | participant)
```

The predictor-by-site interaction models added one `site × context` block at a time while
holding the other two contexts additive. This is the prespecified
lower-dimensional implementation of the proposed
`site * day type + site * activity + site * sleep duration` structure. It
preserves all three main context terms but evaluates each interaction block
without conditioning it on two other high-dimensional interaction blocks.
The four timing outcomes used the corresponding fixed-site linear
models with participant-cluster HC3 covariance. L10 mean remained the named
non-estimable slot 3 and was not replaced. The analysis therefore contributed
14 estimable metrics to six new exploratory 15-slot FDR families.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h06-daily-joint-family-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Exploratory mutually adjusted daily-model FDR families."

joint_family_summary |>
  mutate(
    Predictor = .data$predictor,
    Test = recode(
      .data$test_type,
      conditional_association = "Conditional association",
      conditional_site_heterogeneity = "Conditional predictor-by-site interaction"
    )
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Predictor,
    Test,
    `Named slots` = .data$named_slots,
    `Estimable slots` = .data$estimable_slots,
    `Named NA slots` = .data$named_na_slots,
    `FDR-supported` = .data$fdr_supported_slots,
    `Family valid` = if_else(.data$family_valid, "Yes", "No")
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    groupname_col = "Predictor",
    source_note = paste(
      "Batch: exploratory mutually adjusted near-eye participant-day models.",
      "The numerical work/free interaction count includes MDER, which remains",
      "descriptive because of its major heavy-tail and site-influence limitation."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::cols_align(
    "center",
    columns = c(`Named slots`, `Estimable slots`, `Named NA slots`, `FDR-supported`, `Family valid`)
  )
```

Conditional associations met the exploratory FDR rule for 10 metrics for
Work/Free day, 6 for activity, and 10 for sleep. All 14 activity estimates
shifted by less than one common-sample standard error after adjustment. For
sleep, 11 were stable and 3 shifted by 1 to less than 2 standard errors. For
Work/Free day, 9 were stable, 4 shifted by 1 to less than 2 standard errors,
and the sleep-environment duration estimate reversed direction with a 3.37
standard-error shift. The table shows every substantial or unstable shift;
the remaining estimable cells were stable by the prespecified rule.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h06-daily-joint-stability-limitations
#| tbl-cap: "Covariate-adjustment shifts of at least one common-sample standard error."
#| column: page

joint_stability |>
  filter(
    .data$metric_slot != 3L,
    .data$covariate_stability != "STABLE_LT_1_SE"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Metric = .data$manuscript_name,
    Predictor = .data$predictor,
    `Same rows, predictor-specific` = format_joint_effect(
      .data$display_estimate_common_sample_predictor_specific,
      .data$display_lower_95_common_sample_predictor_specific,
      .data$display_upper_95_common_sample_predictor_specific,
      .data$effect_scale,
      .data$metric_slot
    ),
    `Mutually adjusted` = format_joint_effect(
      .data$display_estimate_mutually_adjusted_joint,
      .data$display_lower_95_mutually_adjusted_joint,
      .data$display_upper_95_mutually_adjusted_joint,
      .data$effect_scale,
      .data$metric_slot
    ),
    `Shift in common-sample SE` = sprintf("%.2f", .data$covariate_shift_in_common_se),
    Assessment = recode(
      .data$covariate_stability,
      SUBSTANTIAL_LIMITATION_1_TO_LT_2_SE = "Substantial limitation",
      UNSTABLE_GE_2_SE_OR_DIRECTION_REVERSAL = "Unstable; direction reversal"
    ),
    `Conditional FDR q` = format_p(.data$conditional_association_bh_q)
  ) |>
  select(
    Predictor,
    Metric,
    `Same rows, predictor-specific`,
    `Mutually adjusted`,
    `Shift in common-sample SE`,
    Assessment,
    `Conditional FDR q`
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    groupname_col = "Predictor",
    source_note = paste(
      "Intervals are pointwise 95% CIs. A shift below 1 SE was stable,",
      "1 to less than 2 SE was a substantial limitation, and at least 2 SE",
      "or a direction reversal was unstable. These are exploratory models."
    ),
    font_size = 9.5
  ) |>
  gt::cols_align(
    "center",
    columns = c(
      `Same rows, predictor-specific`,
      `Mutually adjusted`,
      `Shift in common-sample SE`,
      `Conditional FDR q`
    )
  )
```

Mean melEDI illustrates the distinction. On the same 715-day frame, the
predictor-specific Free/Work ratio was 0.69. It was 0.75 (95% CI 0.68 to
0.82; FDR q < 0.001) after simultaneous adjustment for activity and sleep.
The association therefore attenuated by 1.65 common-sample standard errors
but remained below 1. Activity changed by only 0.11 standard errors, while
the sleep estimate changed by 1.49 standard errors.

Five work/free interaction blocks remained conditionally FDR-supported among
the daily metrics: mean melEDI, brightest 10 h mean, waking time above 250 lx
melEDI, longest continuous period above 250 lx melEDI, and melEDI dose. The
numerical MDER interaction also crossed its exploratory FDR threshold but is
descriptive only because of its major model-check limitation. No conditional
activity or sleep interaction block met the exploratory FDR rule.
As in the primary interaction table, every listed site value is the complete
Free/Work contrast from that interaction model while activity and sleep remain
in the model. It is not an interaction coefficient that needs multiplication
by the joint model's site-average contrast.

```{r}

#| tbl-cap: "Site-specific contrasts for conditionally supported exploratory interaction blocks."
#| column: page

joint_site_summary |>

  ) |>

    `Full Free/Work ratio lower; pointwise 95% CI excludes 1`,
    `Full Free/Work ratio higher; pointwise 95% CI excludes 1`,
    `Full Free/Work ratio; pointwise 95% CI includes 1`,
    Role
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste(
      "Batch: exploratory mutually adjusted near-eye interaction models.",
      "The global interaction q-value is multiplicity adjusted within a 15-slot",
      "family. Site intervals are pointwise and unadjusted. Each value is the",
      "full site-specific Free/Work ratio, not a multiplier to apply to a",
      "separate main effect. Filled dots use consistent study-site colors and do not",
      "encode significance."
    ),
    font_size = 8.7
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = gt::everything()) |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Metric ~ gt::px(200),
    `Conditional interaction FDR q` ~ gt::px(105),
    `Full Free/Work ratio lower; pointwise 95% CI excludes 1` ~ gt::px(330),
    `Full Free/Work ratio higher; pointwise 95% CI excludes 1` ~ gt::px(300),

    Role ~ gt::px(180)

```

For conditionally adjusted mean melEDI, the Free/Work point estimates remained
below 1 at all nine sites. Pointwise intervals excluded 1 at Madrid (ES), 0.45
(95% CI 0.34 to 0.58), and Kumasi (GH), 0.44 (0.34 to 0.58). The other seven
site intervals included 1.
These full site ratios already include the jointly adjusted day-type term and
the corresponding site interaction contribution.

[Complete common-sample stability results](../../artifacts/11_source_data/H06_daily/H06_daily_joint_context_exploratory_stability.csv) and [conditional site estimates](../../artifacts/11_source_data/H06_daily/H06_daily_joint_context_exploratory_site_estimates.csv)

## Exploratory 30-minute time-of-day GAMM

This separate analysis asks how the **shape of the 24-hour profile** varies by
day type, activity, and sleep. It is not a daily-metric sensitivity. The
response is the 30-minute arithmetic mean melEDI, $Y$, transformed as
$\log_{10}(Y + 0.1\ \mathrm{lx})$. Its 33,057 supported half-hour bins come
from 715 participant-days, 137 participants, and all nine sites.

The accepted `mgcv::bam()` model used Gaussian identity errors, fREML,
`discrete = TRUE`, one thread, and a frame-specific working AR(1) coefficient.
This working correlation allows adjacent residuals within each audited
participant-day sequence to be correlated.
Its exact smooth structure was:

```text
s(time, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
s(time, day type, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
s(time, activity, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
s(time, by = between-participant sleep, k = 12) +
s(time, by = within-participant sleep, k = 12) +
s(time, site, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
s(time, participant, bs = "fs", k = 10) +
s(participant-day, bs = "re")
```

Only the global time smooth used the cyclic cubic basis. The `sz`, `fs`, and
sleep time margins retained mgcv's default thin-plate basis, with no cyclic
`xt` request. Sleep was separated into the participant mean and the day's
deviation from that mean.

![Time-varying near-eye context associations from the exploratory 30-minute GAMM. Curves are ratios for fitted Y plus 0.1 lx; bands are pointwise 95% confidence intervals.](../../artifacts/10_figures/H06_daily/H06_daily_temporal_h02_primary_context_functions.png){#fig-h06-daily-temporal-gamm fig-alt="Four-panel time-of-day figure for the primary near-eye 30-minute GAMM. Curves show ratios for fitted melEDI plus 0.1 lx across 48 half-hour midpoints for Free versus Work day, Active versus Sedentary status, one additional hour of within-participant sleep, and one additional hour of between-participant mean sleep. Pointwise 95 percent bands accompany each curve and a horizontal line marks ratio one." width="100%"}

[Source data for the temporal GAMM figure](../../artifacts/11_source_data/H06_daily/H06_daily_temporal_h02_primary_context_functions_figure_source.csv)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h06-daily-temporal-gamm
#| tbl-cap: "Exploratory primary near-eye 30-minute GAMM summaries."

temporal_gamm |>
  mutate(
    Estimand = .data$estimand_label,
    `Ratio range over day` = sprintf(
      "%.2f to %.2f",
      .data$minimum_shifted_response_ratio,
      .data$maximum_shifted_response_ratio
    ),
    `Strongest fitted association` = sprintf(
      "%s: %.2f times",
      format_clock_time(.data$time_of_maximum_absolute_association_h),
      .data$ratio_at_maximum_absolute_association
    ),
    `Pointwise intervals excluding 1` = paste0(
      .data$pointwise_bins_excluding_null,
      " / ",
      .data$evaluated_half_hour_midpoints
    ),
    `Whole-function FDR q` = paste0("**", format_p(.data$bh_adjusted_p_value), "**")
  ) |>
  select(
    Estimand,
    `Ratio range over day`,
    `Strongest fitted association`,
    `Pointwise intervals excluding 1`,
    `Whole-function FDR q`
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste(
      "Ratios refer to fitted Y + 0.1 lx, not the raw-scale arithmetic mean Y.",
      "The q-values are approximate whole-function tests in one four-test FDR",
      "family. All displayed curve intervals are pointwise, not simultaneous."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = `Whole-function FDR q`) |>
  gt::cols_align(
    "center",
    columns = c(
      `Ratio range over day`,
      `Strongest fitted association`,
      `Pointwise intervals excluding 1`,
      `Whole-function FDR q`
    )
  )
```

All four whole-function tests met the exploratory FDR rule. The Free/Work
ratio was lowest at 08:45, 0.20, but exceeded 1 after midnight, reaching 1.84.
The Active/Sedentary ratio reached 1.62 at 15:15. One additional hour of sleep
within participant was most strongly associated at 00:15, ratio 0.76. One
additional hour of participant-mean sleep had its strongest fitted association
at 08:45, ratio 0.61. These are time-varying observational associations on the
shifted-response scale, not causal effects or raw melEDI ratios.

## Comparison with the selected main H06 analysis

The selected main H06 analysis and this complementary analysis do not estimate
the same quantity. Main H06 gives each supported participant-hour one row and
models the zero-aware geometric mean melEDI for that hour, with all three
contexts in one model. H06_daily gives each admissible participant-day one row
per metric. Its primary models are predictor-specific, while the exploratory
joint column below uses a common 715-day frame and includes all three contexts.
Where a global predictor-by-site interaction met its FDR rule, the table uses
the **site-average full contrast from that interaction model**, with every site
weighted equally, and gives the
range of its nine full site-specific ratios. Otherwise it uses the additive
model's common contrast. The additive-family association q-value remains the
prespecified association test, while the global interaction q-value determines
which effect model is displayed.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h06-daily-main-comparison
#| tbl-cap: "Selected main hourly H06 versus daily mean-melEDI associations."
#| column: page

main_hourly_comparison |>
  mutate(
    Context = .data$predictor,
    `Main hourly H06, jointly adjusted` = format_comparison_model_cell(
      .data$hourly_selected_estimate,
      .data$hourly_selected_lower_95,
      .data$hourly_selected_upper_95,
      .data$hourly_uses_interaction,
      .data$hourly_interaction_site_minimum,
      .data$hourly_interaction_site_maximum,
      .data$hourly_association_bh_q,
      .data$hourly_site_heterogeneity_bh_q
    ),
    `Daily mean, predictor-specific` = format_comparison_model_cell(
      .data$daily_predictor_specific_selected_estimate,
      .data$daily_predictor_specific_selected_lower_95,
      .data$daily_predictor_specific_selected_upper_95,
      .data$daily_predictor_specific_uses_interaction,
      .data$daily_predictor_specific_interaction_site_minimum,
      .data$daily_predictor_specific_interaction_site_maximum,
      .data$daily_predictor_specific_bh_q,
      .data$daily_predictor_specific_site_bh_q
    ),
    `Daily mean, mutually adjusted exploratory` = format_comparison_model_cell(
      .data$daily_joint_selected_estimate,
      .data$daily_joint_selected_lower_95,
      .data$daily_joint_selected_upper_95,
      .data$daily_joint_uses_interaction,
      .data$daily_joint_interaction_site_minimum,
      .data$daily_joint_interaction_site_maximum,
      .data$daily_joint_bh_q,
      .data$daily_joint_site_bh_q
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    Context,
    `Main hourly H06, jointly adjusted`,
    `Daily mean, predictor-specific`,
    `Daily mean, mutually adjusted exploratory`
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste(
      "All entries are site-average ratios, with sites weighted equally, and pointwise 95% CIs, but their",
      "outcomes, weighting, fitted samples, model families, and multiplicity",
      "families differ. Supported interaction rows use the site-average geometric",
      "mean of the nine full site-specific ratios from that model and show the",
      "site range. Other rows use the additive common contrast. Interaction-model",
      "site ratios are full contrasts and require no multiplication by a main",
      "effect. Numerical equality is neither expected nor claimed."
    ),
    font_size = 9.5
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = -Context) |>
  gt::cols_width(Context ~ gt::px(170), gt::everything() ~ gt::px(280))
```

The clearest contrast is day type, for which all three global site interactions
were supported. The interaction-model site-average ratio was 1.15 (95% CI 0.93
to 1.44) in main hourly H06, with full site-specific ratios from 0.53 to 2.44.
Daily mean melEDI was lower on Free days in both the predictor-specific
interaction model, site-average ratio 0.70 (0.63 to 0.78; site range 0.40 to
0.95), and the mutually adjusted interaction model, 0.73 (0.66 to 0.81; site
range 0.44 to 1.00). This is not a failed replication. The hourly analysis
weights days by their supported hours and targets a retained hour's geometric
mean; the daily analysis weights admissible days equally and targets a daily
metric.

Activity was positive in all three analyses. Its primary daily interaction was
supported, so that column uses the interaction-model site-average ratio 1.22
(1.08 to 1.39; full site ratios 0.84 to 2.26). The main hourly and mutually
adjusted daily activity interactions were not supported, so their displayed
2.06 and 1.16 ratios come from additive models. Previous sleep had no supported
site interaction in any column. It was compatible with little hourly
association, additive ratio 0.98 and FDR q = 0.745, but was associated with
lower daily mean melEDI, additive ratios 0.89 and 0.90. The analyses therefore
provide related but non-interchangeable evidence about hourly exposure and
participant-day metrics.

## Model checks and limitations

### Primary and gap-sensitivity daily grid

All 468 non-L10 model cells passed the hard construct, support, numerical, and
estimability gates, but every cell was classified **acceptable with
limitations** after direct visual review of residual centering, variance, and
gross distributional shape. No gross residual failure was observed.

Temporal dependence was retained as a mandatory model-check sidecar rather than an
automatic failure criterion. Actual-date AR counterparts were sometimes
singular, numerically unresolved, or left residual dependence; those findings
remain part of interpretation but do not replace the primary estimates or
p-values. In the primary timing route, the first-light Work/Free Student-t
estimate shifted by 1.23 participant-cluster HC3 standard errors, and the L10
midpoint activity AR estimate shifted by 1.26 HC3 standard errors. Timing
predictor-by-site results remain sensitivity-dependent.

Participant/site deletion checks were stable for 270 of 468 cells, showed a
substantial limitation for 128, were unstable for 46, and had a non-estimable
deletion refit for 24. Gaussian, Tweedie, Student-t, exact-period, and AR
model-check sidecars are reported as response-family or stability limitations; none was
used to substitute a p-value. MDER additionally retains its heavy-tail and
site-influence qualifications.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h06-daily-diagnostic-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Model-check and sensitivity classifications."

diagnostic_summary |>
  mutate(
    Domain = .data$domain,
    Classification = .data$reader_classification,
    Role = .data$reporting_role
  ) |>
  transmute(Domain, Classification, Cells = .data$cells, Role) |>
  compact_gt(
    groupname_col = "Domain",
    source_note = paste(
      "Residual review and hard construct/support/numerical checks determine",
      "overall usability. AR, influence, family, and exact-period rows are",
      "mandatory nonblocking limitation sidecars under the analysis rule."
    ),
    font_size = 10.5
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = Cells) |>
  gt::cols_align("center", columns = Cells)
```

### Exploratory mutually adjusted daily models

All 14 estimable joint models and their required additive and one-interaction
structures were numerically estimable. Direct residual-plot review classified
all 14 as review limitations and none as a gross failure. First-light timing
retained a U-shaped residual pattern and heavy tails under the participant-HC3
route. MDER retained pronounced upper-tail and site-influence limitations.
Actual-date residual lag was reported descriptively and did not replace or
invalidate an otherwise usable model. No deletion batch, bootstrap, or
simulation was added to this exploratory analysis.

### Exploratory temporal GAMM

Five of six fitted frames met the accepted formula, convergence, basis,
residual, temporal-dependence, fixed-term-identifiability, and cyclic-closure
rules. All six BAM fits converged without fitting warnings, but the paired
chest frame did not meet the residual-scale extraction rule and contributed no
association summary. In the primary near-eye fit, the residual Q-Q correlation
was 0.965, the absolute-residual/fitted Spearman correlation was 0.293, final
pooled lag-1 correlation was 0.090, and the largest absolute site lag-1
correlation was 0.159. The bounded `k = 16` check supported retaining `k = 12`.
Participant and site deletion robustness remains untested for the GAMM, so its
results stay exploratory.

These are observational associations with recorded day-level contexts. They
do not establish causal effects, health outcomes, identical associations
across sites, or equivalence between sensor placements.
